items.title: Marian McPartland — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: when I was playing with this other pianist, Romer [spelling?] Clark

ctx.x: At that point. Professionally at least not.

At that point. I was playing a kind of a mish-mash of stuff. When we were playing in these . . . when I was playing with this other pianist, Romer [spelling?] Clark, we would play little symphonic arrangements, cocktaily arrangements. They were nice, but they weren’t jazz. Then the things that I would do for a while, let’s see . . . for Carroll Levis, I would play . . . wait a minute. I think I’m losing my own chronology here. I think I went with Carroll Levis after war was declared. In fact I did, because I…
You were a freelancer in a sense.
